key_themes: Brand refresh initiative launched with new visual identity 'Fortuna Wave' representing Authenticity, Prosperity, and Togetherness (APT) to enhance recognition and attract newer audiences through digital channels
Strategic investment from Blackstone received board, shareholder, and CCI approval, providing capital strengthening and access to global institutional expertise for long-term growth
Liability franchise transformation showing strong CASA growth of 6.59% QoQ and 18.86% YoY, with CASA ratio improving to 32.07% (up 106 bps QoQ), among best in industry
Shift toward mid-yield assets with commercial banking growing 26% YoY and business banking showing recovery at 3.82% QoQ growth after earlier year muted performance
Margin expansion journey continuing with NIM at 3.18% (up 12 bps QoQ) driven by liability mix optimization, asset repricing, and funding cost reduction despite 125 bps rate cuts over past year
Structural improvements in asset and liability mix with focus on CASA growth (especially current accounts) and mid-yielding assets over low-yielding corporate and home loans
NIM expansion driven by deposit cost reduction (19 bps) and improved CASA ratio up 100+ bps Q-o-Q, exceeding earlier guidance at 3.06%
Asset quality stabilization with MFI stress peaking but not yet in comfortable zone; credit cost moderated to 50 bps from 65 bps
Selective growth strategy focusing on profitable segments (commercial banking at 20%+ growth, cards, gold loans at 7% Q-o-Q) while deliberately rationalizing low-yield assets
Fee income diversification showing resilience with 13% Q-o-Q growth and fee-to-assets crossing 1% milestone despite muted treasury income

Federal 4.0 transformation strategy focused on three pillars: improving CASA (especially current accounts), driving better yield on advances through asset mix reshaping, and increasing granular fee income
Branch transformation through 'Free The Branch' initiative with 70 regional business support centers created to allow frontline teams to focus on relationship building and sourcing
Technology backbone upgrades including GenAI-powered chatbot, FedOne corporate interface launch, corporate credit underwriting automation, and IT architecture review with external partner
Organizational restructuring with separate verticals for secured/unsecured retail, B-FIG segment, wealth management and banca vertical fully staffed, and new global transaction banking leadership
MFI and Agri portfolio stress in Q1 with slippages peaking in May and declining trajectory seen in June-July, outside these segments asset quality remained stable or improved
Strategic focus on mid-yielding segments (mass affluent, MSME, LAP, gold loans) to drive sustainable profitability with 19% Y-o-Y growth achieved
Significant improvement in liability franchise with CASA growing 6.74% Q-o-Q, CA growth at 27% Q-o-Q and 35% Y-o-Y on retail and wholesale fronts
Asset quality at decadal best with GNPA at 1.84% (down 11 bps Q-o-Q), NNPA at 0.44%, and provision coverage strengthened to 75.37%
Operational transformation initiatives including new transfer pricing methodology, RaRoC-based pricing model, business P&L system, and Operation Udaan to modernize branch operations
Crossed INR5 lakh crore business milestone with net profit exceeding INR4,000 crores, driven by robust fee income growth of 6% Q-o-Q outpacing asset growth
management_outlook: NIM expansion is a journey not yet complete, with continued improvement expected over many quarters as CASA percentage grows and medium-yield assets grow faster than low-yield assets, though next quarter will see impact of recent rate cut
Credit costs expected to improve to 52-53 bps for full year FY26 versus 55-60 bps initial guidance, with Q4 expected to be lower than Q3's 47 bps as MFI portfolio stabilizes
MFI segment showing improvement each quarter in slippages and credit costs, but management remains cautious and will selectively grow for one more quarter before accelerating growth

Too early to provide quantitative targets for loan mix in 3-5 years, but strategy remains to grow mid-yield book faster than high-yield book while maintaining discipline on unsecured segments like personal loans
Medium-term credit costs guidance unchanged as growth in medium-yield assets will carry higher credit costs than low-yield corporate book which has near-zero credit costs
Confident about further NIM improvement beyond 3.06% as deposits continue repricing over next 6 months and CASA momentum sustains
Expect stronger growth in LAP, BuB, auto loans and tractor business in coming quarters after reversing negative trends to support full year guidance
Maintaining full year credit cost guidance at 55 bps despite Q2 improvement to 50 bps, awaiting more comfort on MFI portfolio stabilization
Remittance market share recovered from 18.5% to 21% showing renewed momentum in core NRI franchise
Asset quality remains rock solid outside of MFI segment with no concerns in other business lines
NIM expected to bottom out in Q2 (subject to no further rate cuts) and improve in H2 as cost of funds falls, with T+1 repricing already reflecting 100 bps rate cut impact
Credit cost guidance maintained at around 55 bps for full year, with MFI stress expected to linger at best one more quarter due to accelerated provisioning policy taking 100% provision
Advance growth expected to accelerate in H2 with festive season and post-monsoon disbursement momentum, targeting growth at 1.2x nominal GDP
Strong opportunities seen in secured MSME, business banking, gold-backed lending, LAP and CVCE as medium-yielding segments with risk-adjusted profitability focus
Federal 4.0 transformation is multi-quarter journey with over 50 large and 100 small projects under execution, may experience some air pockets but execution remains resolute
Confident in achieving high-teen loan growth in FY26 driven by resumed gold loan growth post regulatory clarity, cards momentum, personal loan revival, and mid-market corporate acquisitions
NIM management strategy includes resetting floating loans at T+90 instead of T+1, shifting car loans to fixed rates, and offering medium-tenure fixed loans to maintain stability amid rate cuts
Strong talent acquisition with 9 of 14 key N-2 positions filled including new ED Virat Diwanji, positioning for enhanced strategic execution capabilities
Cautious approach to high-yield segments with microfinance requiring 1-2 more quarters of prudence, while personal loans expected to resume growth as credit environment stabilizes
LCR improved to 145% through degrowth of wholesale deposits from financial entities, demonstrating balanced growth and strong liquidity management
analyst_concerns: Sustainability of margin expansion going forward given already strong 24 bps improvement over last two quarters and where margins will stabilize in medium to long term
Impact of recent rate cut on margins with questions about timing of repricing, with clarification that one-third impact in Q3 and two-thirds will play out in Q4
Distribution fee income weakness this quarter and reasons behind it, with concerns about sequential decline despite overall fee income growth
MFI credit costs currently at 10-11% and trajectory going forward, with questions about when this segment will fully recover and normalize
Asset quality outlook for MSME segment and potential impact from US tariffs or broader economic uncertainty on commercial and business banking portfolios
Low loan growth at 1.5% Q-o-Q (half of system growth) and ability to meet 1.2x nominal GDP growth target given 50% of book in low-yielding segments
Sustainability of CASA ratio improvement once overall balance sheet growth accelerates, as current growth is also helping the ratio
MFI stress persistence despite peaking last quarter, with slippages still not in comfortable zone and continued provisioning impact
Rationale for potential capital raise given margin improvements and ability to self-fund through internal accruals
Impact of upcoming RBI guidelines on ECL provisions and operational/credit risk standardized approach on capital ratios
MFI stress bunching up in Q1 versus peers recognizing it in Q3-Q4, with questions about aging provisions on slippages and whether credit costs will remain elevated in Q2
Stress build-up in retail segments including unsecured, business banking, CV, and MFI with concerns about new stress emerging across multiple lenders in the industry
NIM compression due to faster T+1 repricing on advances while deposit repricing lags, with questions about quantum of further decline in Q2 before stabilization
Branch expansion may be slower this year due to scientific assessment and redesign work, raising questions about near-term distribution growth momentum
Intense competition on pricing in the market with concerns about balancing growth aspirations with risk-adjusted profitability discipline
NIM pressure from expected repo rate cuts given high EBLR-linked book proportion (over 50%), with analyst seeking clarity on margin floor levels for FY26
Sustainability and stickiness of year-end CASA growth, particularly current account growth, given other banks' experience with non-sticky year-end deposits
One-off costs in Q4 opex related to 39 branch openings, campaign advertisements and card campaigns leading to elevated cost-to-income ratio

concall_themes: Brand refresh initiative launched with new visual identity 'Fortuna Wave' representing Authenticity, Prosperity, and Togetherness (APT) to enhance recognition and attract newer audiences through digital channels
Strategic investment from Blackstone received board, shareholder, and CCI approval, providing capital strengthening and access to global institutional expertise for long-term growth
Liability franchise transformation showing strong CASA growth of 6.59% QoQ and 18.86% YoY, with CASA ratio improving to 32.07% (up 106 bps QoQ), among best in industry
Shift toward mid-yield assets with commercial banking growing 26% YoY and business banking showing recovery at 3.82% QoQ growth after earlier year muted performance
Margin expansion journey continuing with NIM at 3.18% (up 12 bps QoQ) driven by liability mix optimization, asset repricing, and funding cost reduction despite 125 bps rate cuts over past year
Structural improvements in asset and liability mix with focus on CASA growth (especially current accounts) and mid-yielding assets over low-yielding corporate and home loans
NIM expansion driven by deposit cost reduction (19 bps) and improved CASA ratio up 100+ bps Q-o-Q, exceeding earlier guidance at 3.06%
Asset quality stabilization with MFI stress peaking but not yet in comfortable zone; credit cost moderated to 50 bps from 65 bps
Selective growth strategy focusing on profitable segments (commercial banking at 20%+ growth, cards, gold loans at 7% Q-o-Q) while deliberately rationalizing low-yield assets
Fee income diversification showing resilience with 13% Q-o-Q growth and fee-to-assets crossing 1% milestone despite muted treasury income

Federal 4.0 transformation strategy focused on three pillars: improving CASA (especially current accounts), driving better yield on advances through asset mix reshaping, and increasing granular fee income
Branch transformation through 'Free The Branch' initiative with 70 regional business support centers created to allow frontline teams to focus on relationship building and sourcing
Technology backbone upgrades including GenAI-powered chatbot, FedOne corporate interface launch, corporate credit underwriting automation, and IT architecture review with external partner
Organizational restructuring with separate verticals for secured/unsecured retail, B-FIG segment, wealth management and banca vertical fully staffed, and new global transaction banking leadership
MFI and Agri portfolio stress in Q1 with slippages peaking in May and declining trajectory seen in June-July, outside these segments asset quality remained stable or improved
Strategic focus on mid-yielding segments (mass affluent, MSME, LAP, gold loans) to drive sustainable profitability with 19% Y-o-Y growth achieved
Significant improvement in liability franchise with CASA growing 6.74% Q-o-Q, CA growth at 27% Q-o-Q and 35% Y-o-Y on retail and wholesale fronts
Asset quality at decadal best with GNPA at 1.84% (down 11 bps Q-o-Q), NNPA at 0.44%, and provision coverage strengthened to 75.37%
Operational transformation initiatives including new transfer pricing methodology, RaRoC-based pricing model, business P&L system, and Operation Udaan to modernize branch operations
Crossed INR5 lakh crore business milestone with net profit exceeding INR4,000 crores, driven by robust fee income growth of 6% Q-o-Q outpacing asset growth
analyst_concerns: Sustainability of margin expansion going forward given already strong 24 bps improvement over last two quarters and where margins will stabilize in medium to long term
Impact of recent rate cut on margins with questions about timing of repricing, with clarification that one-third impact in Q3 and two-thirds will play out in Q4
Distribution fee income weakness this quarter and reasons behind it, with concerns about sequential decline despite overall fee income growth
MFI credit costs currently at 10-11% and trajectory going forward, with questions about when this segment will fully recover and normalize
Asset quality outlook for MSME segment and potential impact from US tariffs or broader economic uncertainty on commercial and business banking portfolios
Low loan growth at 1.5% Q-o-Q (half of system growth) and ability to meet 1.2x nominal GDP growth target given 50% of book in low-yielding segments
Sustainability of CASA ratio improvement once overall balance sheet growth accelerates, as current growth is also helping the ratio
MFI stress persistence despite peaking last quarter, with slippages still not in comfortable zone and continued provisioning impact
Rationale for potential capital raise given margin improvements and ability to self-fund through internal accruals
Impact of upcoming RBI guidelines on ECL provisions and operational/credit risk standardized approach on capital ratios
MFI stress bunching up in Q1 versus peers recognizing it in Q3-Q4, with questions about aging provisions on slippages and whether credit costs will remain elevated in Q2
Stress build-up in retail segments including unsecured, business banking, CV, and MFI with concerns about new stress emerging across multiple lenders in the industry
NIM compression due to faster T+1 repricing on advances while deposit repricing lags, with questions about quantum of further decline in Q2 before stabilization
Branch expansion may be slower this year due to scientific assessment and redesign work, raising questions about near-term distribution growth momentum
Intense competition on pricing in the market with concerns about balancing growth aspirations with risk-adjusted profitability discipline
NIM pressure from expected repo rate cuts given high EBLR-linked book proportion (over 50%), with analyst seeking clarity on margin floor levels for FY26
Sustainability and stickiness of year-end CASA growth, particularly current account growth, given other banks' experience with non-sticky year-end deposits
One-off costs in Q4 opex related to 39 branch openings, campaign advertisements and card campaigns leading to elevated cost-to-income ratio
Growth trajectory uncertainty given muted home loan growth and cautious microfinance approach, questioning ability to return to high-teen loan growth
Impact of gold loan regulatory headwinds in Q4 on overall mid-yield segment momentum going forward
management_outlook: NIM expansion is a journey not yet complete, with continued improvement expected over many quarters as CASA percentage grows and medium-yield assets grow faster than low-yield assets, though next quarter will see impact of recent rate cut
Credit costs expected to improve to 52-53 bps for full year FY26 versus 55-60 bps initial guidance, with Q4 expected to be lower than Q3's 47 bps as MFI portfolio stabilizes
MFI segment showing improvement each quarter in slippages and credit costs, but management remains cautious and will selectively grow for one more quarter before accelerating growth

Too early to provide quantitative targets for loan mix in 3-5 years, but strategy remains to grow mid-yield book faster than high-yield book while maintaining discipline on unsecured segments like personal loans
Medium-term credit costs guidance unchanged as growth in medium-yield assets will carry higher credit costs than low-yield corporate book which has near-zero credit costs
Confident about further NIM improvement beyond 3.06% as deposits continue repricing over next 6 months and CASA momentum sustains
Expect stronger growth in LAP, BuB, auto loans and tractor business in coming quarters after reversing negative trends to support full year guidance
Maintaining full year credit cost guidance at 55 bps despite Q2 improvement to 50 bps, awaiting more comfort on MFI portfolio stabilization
Remittance market share recovered from 18.5% to 21% showing renewed momentum in core NRI franchise
Asset quality remains rock solid outside of MFI segment with no concerns in other business lines
NIM expected to bottom out in Q2 (subject to no further rate cuts) and improve in H2 as cost of funds falls, with T+1 repricing already reflecting 100 bps rate cut impact
Credit cost guidance maintained at around 55 bps for full year, with MFI stress expected to linger at best one more quarter due to accelerated provisioning policy taking 100% provision
Advance growth expected to accelerate in H2 with festive season and post-monsoon disbursement momentum, targeting growth at 1.2x nominal GDP
Strong opportunities seen in secured MSME, business banking, gold-backed lending, LAP and CVCE as medium-yielding segments with risk-adjusted profitability focus
Federal 4.0 transformation is multi-quarter journey with over 50 large and 100 small projects under execution, may experience some air pockets but execution remains resolute
Confident in achieving high-teen loan growth in FY26 driven by resumed gold loan growth post regulatory clarity, cards momentum, personal loan revival, and mid-market corporate acquisitions
NIM management strategy includes resetting floating loans at T+90 instead of T+1, shifting car loans to fixed rates, and offering medium-tenure fixed loans to maintain stability amid rate cuts
Strong talent acquisition with 9 of 14 key N-2 positions filled including new ED Virat Diwanji, positioning for enhanced strategic execution capabilities
Cautious approach to high-yield segments with microfinance requiring 1-2 more quarters of prudence, while personal loans expected to resume growth as credit environment stabilizes
LCR improved to 145% through degrowth of wholesale deposits from financial entities, demonstrating balanced growth and strong liquidity management
